title: 2019_PMC6668241_Identification_of_the_determinants_of_incomplete_vaccination_in_
ehr_evidence: Vaccination status was determined from the Australian Childhood Immunisation Register and deemed either “complete” (no doses overdue) or “incomplete” (1 or more doses overdue) at the time of questionnaire completion.
summary: Cross-sectional study assessing sociodemographic and parental belief factors associated with incomplete childhood vaccination status in Western Australia.
key_findings: 20% (116/589) of children had incomplete vaccination status.
Children with incomplete status were more likely born overseas (OR: 3.52, 95% CI: 1.54 to 8.05).
More likely to have a healthcare professional advise delaying or not vaccinating (OR: 4.25, 95% CI: 2.07 to 8.69).
Associated with lower parental education (<Year 10 high school) (OR: 2.92, 95% CI: 1.34 to 6.39).
Associated with larger family size (OR: 1.39 per child increase, 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.87).
No significant association between parental beliefs/attitudes and vaccination status remained after adjusting for sociodemographic factors.
population: children <6 years old attending outpatient clinics in Perth, Western Australia, and their parents
exposure_domain: sociodemographic factors, parental beliefs, healthcare access
limitations: convenience sample from hospital setting may underrepresent high SES, fathers, and ethnic minorities
self-reported survey data subject to recall and social desirability bias
immunisation register may not accurately reflect status for overseas-born children
unverified healthcare professional advice on vaccine delay
